plan: [In a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values, the dominant strategy is truthful bidding. Other bidders are rational and face the same logic, so bidding my true value maximizes expected surplus: if I win I pay the second-highest bid, keeping value minus price nonnegative on average. Ties are random; slightly shading risks losing positive-surplus wins. Therefore I will bid my private value: $9. ]

[This is a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values. In a Vickrey auction, bidding my true value is a dominant strategy: I maximize expected payoff by bidding $20 regardless of others' strategies. Ties are random but truthful bidding remains optimal. Therefore submit bid equal to my value.]

[This is a second-price sealed-bid auction; bidding your true private value is a dominant strategy and maximizes expected payoff regardless of opponents' strategies. Values are independent each round and ties are resolved randomly, so bid exactly your value (rounded to the allowed increment) to win whenever the second-highest bid is below your value and pay that second-highest price, ensuring nonnegative surplus in expectation.]
